note: Lighting presets. Tune here and re-shoot with tools/lookdev/shoot.sh; never hardcode these in scripts. Azimuth 0 = looking out from the port into the desert (-Z), positive = to the right.
day_order_note: Issue #381 (src/systems/world/day_clock.gd): on Auto the day steps along this list, round and round, each time you go indoors (a cantina, the cruiser), take a faded trip to another planet or wake in the pit. A step never lands on the time you are in, and comes only once day_min_seconds of play have gone by since the last one.
hours_note: Continuous time of day (F11 demo settings): the hour blends between these presets. Before the first and after the last key it holds the end preset.

environment.note: Issue #535: the environment numbers every preset shares, read by src/systems/look/look_environment.gd (it keeps no typed-in lighting constants). sdfgi: 5 cascades from 0.4 m reach about 400 m, as far as anyone sees bounce light through the fog (6 reached 1.6 km); bounce_feedback carries light over more than one bounce. shadow_fade_s: the sun's shadows fade out and in over this long when AltitudeDetail's tiers (content/core/planets/types.json 'detail') take or give them. (SDFGI coming back on when landing is quick because project.godot has it converge in 10 frames, not Godot's 30.) shadow_altitude_max: up to this many metres above the ground the sun's shadows reach that much further than the preset's shadow_distance, so the ground under a flying ship stays in the last cascade. Per preset, sun.shadow_* sets the cascades: 600 m in 4 splits at 4%, 12% and 35% (the first cascade 24 m deep), fading from 85%; post.glow_threshold: only what is brighter than this blooms (the sun, lamps and bolts, not lit sand and plaster).

full_graphics.note: Issue #534: what the full look asks for that Low graphics does not. Read by src/systems/look/look_environment.gd. render_scale: with Temporal anti-aliasing on (F11 > Options > Graphics, the default) the 3D world is drawn at this share of the window and brought up by a temporal upscaler (MetalFX on a Mac that offers it, else FSR 2), which is also the anti-aliasing; 0.77 draws ~59% of the pixels. Off, the world is drawn at full size with FXAA. fsr_sharpness: 0 sharpest, 2 softest (Godot's default 0.2). Low graphics' resolution piece wins over both.

low_graphics.note: F11 > Options > Graphics > Low graphics, and its pieces one by one under it (saved per machine in user://settings/graphics.cfg). Read by src/systems/look/look_environment.gd, dust_wind.gd and draw_distance.gd. pieces: what Low graphics changes, each its own checkbox so one can be tried at a time (to find which one stops a glare on one PC). id: the saved key; label: the checkbox; off: render features it holds off (the worlds' 'detail' tier names: sdfgi, ssil, ssao, volumetric, plus glow); low: false for a piece Low graphics leaves alone (bloom is only there to try). The numbers below belong to one piece each. shadows: the sun's shadows end shadow_m metres out (the presets ask for 600), in 2 splits instead of 4. resolution: the 3D world is drawn at render_scale of the window and scaled up with FSR 1, with FXAA on top (0.75 draws ~56% of the pixels; the HUD stays sharp). fill: the sky's fill times ambient, and bounce_share of it from the bounce sand colour instead of the sky, standing in for the warm light SDFGI bounces off the ground. dust: the share of blowing sand still drawn. draw: every range in world.json 'draw_distance' times draw_scale; ranges a system set itself (the barge, the wreck field, the camps') stay as they are.
